content.title: About
content.content: White sangria is a refreshing alcoholic beverage made from dry white wine, fruit juices, sliced fruit, and a touch of sugar or honey. It is typically served chilled, popular in summer and at festive gatherings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sangria originates from Spain, where red wine is traditional; the white version appeared later and became popular in tourist areas.
The classic recipe includes orange, lemon, lime, and apple, but variations may use berries, peaches, or tropical fruits.
White sangria is often served in large pitchers, allowing the fruit to infuse and impart aroma to the drink.
Sangria can be made at home or commercially; the finished product is usually kept refrigerated for up to 3 days.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Fruits used in sangria are rich in vitamin C and polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Moderate consumption may aid hydration
items.content: The high water and fruit juice content supports fluid balance, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: White wine provides small amounts of vitamin B6, involved in protein metabolism.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Sangria contains alcohol and should be consumed responsibly; avoid during pregnancy, driving, or for children.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sugar or honey increases calories; people with diabetes should monitor intake.

items.title: Fruit allergies
items.content: Certain fruits may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve white sangria chilled in glasses or tumblers with fruit pieces. Ice, sparkling water, or a splash of liqueur can be added for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared sangria in a sealed container in the refrigerator for no more than 3–4 days. Stir before serving as sediment may settle at the bottom.
